rules.quote: Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product.
rules.note: Exactly one late product per call in Brief A; days_late 1 to 45.

rules.quote: The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.
rules.note: Stage order: opening -> identity -> debt -> promise -> close.

rules.quote: Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.
rules.note: No account fact (product, amount, days late) may be used or said before get_account returned it.

rules.quote: Pass it to every tool call.
rules.note: customer_id goes into the body of all tool calls: verify_identity, get_account, create_promise, schedule_callback, transfer_to_agent, close_call.

rules.quote: The person to ask for.
rules.note: first_name, last_name.

rules.quote: Address the customer as title plus last name.
rules.note: title is Mr or Ms. Never first name alone.

rules.quote: The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.
rules.note: 'today' = date part of now (example value 2026-10-14T11:00, i.e. 11:00 on 2026-10-14). Code must take now as an input, never read the system clock.

rules.quote: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded.
rules.note: Brief rule 1.

rules.quote: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
rules.note: Brief rule 1. Forbidden words until all_verified is true. Covers third parties too.

rules.quote: Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
rules.note: Brief rule 2.

rules.quote: Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not.
rules.note: Brief rule 3.

rules.quote: Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.
rules.note: Brief rule 3. Counter: at most 2 asks in total, then close_call outcome not_reached reason unclear.

rules.quote: Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.
rules.note: Brief rule 3. Answering a robot/scam question does not give an extra ask.

rules.quote: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
rules.note: Brief rule 4. Any stage; resume where the call was.

rules.quote: Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.
rules.note: Brief rule 5. Section 4 = someone else answers.

rules.quote: Ask when the customer can be reached.
rules.note: Brief rule 5.

rules.quote: A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`.
rules.note: Brief rule 6. Date in {today, next business day after today}; time 10:00..19:00 inclusive; datetime strictly later than now. Business days per the section 7 definition.

rules.quote: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
rules.note: Brief rule 6. API: date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM. The service does not enforce the window; the agent must.

rules.quote: If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
rules.note: Brief rule 7. One re-ask only; no schedule_callback on the no_callback path.

rules.quote: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
rules.note: Brief rule 8.

rules.quote: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.note: Brief rule 9. Exact sentence; no callback question.

rules.quote: A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
rules.note: Brief rule 10. No verify_identity for a third party.

rules.quote: Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file.
rules.note: Brief rule 11. API field values: date_of_birth, then phone_last4 (four digits).

rules.quote: Call `verify_identity` with the answer.
rules.note: Brief rule 11. One call per answer; response has verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified, hint.

rules.quote: Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date.
rules.note: Brief rule 11. API: an unreadable value returns ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer.

rules.quote: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
rules.note: Brief rule 11.

rules.quote: A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
rules.note: Brief rule 12. Shared counter across both questions; API returns wrong_answers_left.

rules.quote: If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
rules.note: Brief rule 13.

rules.quote: After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
rules.note: Brief rule 14. No get_account.

rules.quote: If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.note: Brief rule 15.

rules.quote: Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
rules.note: Brief rule 15. Refusals and 'what is this about' share one counter: first -> explain once, second -> not_verified / declined. The reason for the call still may not be said (rule 1).

rules.quote: After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
rules.note: Brief rule 16. API refuses get_account until both questions are passed. Product type is one of credit_card, personal_loan, car_loan.

rules.quote: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
rules.note: Brief rule 17. credit_card -> 'credit card ending {card_last4}'; never the product_id or the raw enum. Uses past_due and days_late.

rules.quote: Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
rules.note: Holiday table for all date code.

rules.quote: The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
rules.note: Brief rule 18. Keyed on days_late from get_account.

rules.quote: 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1
rules.note: Brief rule 18 table row. Today is not counted. 1 persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2
rules.note: Brief rule 18 table row. Today is not counted. 2 persuasion attempts.

rules.quote: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
rules.note: Brief rule 19. Hard gate on create_promise; the service does not enforce it.

rules.quote: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
rules.note: Brief rule 20.

rules.quote: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
rules.note: Brief rule 21. Ask-once flag.

rules.quote: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
rules.note: Brief rule 22.

rules.quote: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.note: Brief rule 23.

rules.quote: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
rules.note: Brief rule 24.

rules.quote: Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
rules.note: Brief rule 24.

rules.quote: The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
rules.note: Brief rule 25. credit_card -> minimum_payment; personal_loan, car_loan -> instalment_amount.

rules.quote: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue.
rules.note: Brief rule 26. Floor-offered flag.

rules.quote: If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.note: Brief rule 26. Exception to 'once' and to rule 31's no-repeat: attempt 2 (late band).

rules.quote: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
rules.note: Brief rule 27. floor <= amount <= past_due. An amount above past_due is not covered: see open_questions.

rules.quote: Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.note: Brief rule 27.

rules.quote: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
rules.note: Brief rule 28.

rules.quote: A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
rules.note: Brief rule 29. Must not consume a persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
rules.note: Brief rule 30. Attempt counter; limit from the rule 18 band (1 early, 2 late).

rules.quote: Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
rules.note: Brief rule 30.

rules.quote: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.note: Brief rule 30. Usually Friday; earlier if Friday is a holiday.

rules.quote: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
rules.note: Brief rule 30.

rules.quote: When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
rules.note: Brief rule 31.

rules.quote: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
rules.note: Brief rule 32.

rules.quote: If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`.
rules.note: Brief rule 32.

rules.quote: If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.note: Brief rule 32.

rules.quote: This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
rules.note: Brief rule 32. Hardship plus a plan request -> support offer, not restructuring. A customer-named date/amount is still taken as a promise.

rules.quote: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.
rules.note: Brief rule 33.

rules.quote: Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
rules.note: Brief rule 34. create_promise body: customer_id, product_id, amount, date (YYYY-MM-DD).

rules.quote: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
rules.note: Brief rule 35.

rules.quote: One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
rules.note: Brief rule 36. Once-only flag: never a second create_promise after ok: true.

rules.quote: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.
rules.note: Brief rule 37.

rules.quote: If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
rules.note: Brief rule 37. Max 2 create_promise tries. API: failure is ok=false or HTTP 500 (nothing recorded, may be repeated).

rules.quote: After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
rules.note: Brief rule 38. Exact sentence.

rules.quote: "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
rules.note: Brief rule 39. No reason on close_call.

rules.quote: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.
rules.note: Brief rule 40.

rules.quote: A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
rules.note: Brief rule 40.

rules.quote: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
rules.note: Brief rule 41. Rule 32 takes precedence.

rules.quote: A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
rules.note: Brief rule 42. Queue is general but the close reason is human.

rules.quote: "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
rules.note: Brief rule 43. No number is given in the brief: do not invent one.

rules.quote: A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
rules.note: Brief rule 44.

rules.quote: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.note: Brief rule 45.

rules.quote: Rule 42 applies before and after verification.
rules.note: Brief rule 45.

rules.quote: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.
rules.note: Brief rule 46. API: nothing is accepted after close_call; reason required for every outcome except promise and paid.

rules.quote: `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded
rules.note: Close table row.

rules.quote: `paid` | none | rule 39
rules.note: Close table row.

rules.quote: `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32
rules.note: Close table row.

rules.quote: `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37
rules.note: Close table row.

rules.quote: `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15
rules.note: Close table row. Also rule 45 before verification.

rules.quote: `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3
rules.note: Close table row.

rules.quote: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.
rules.note: Overrides outcome promise.

rules.quote: Brief A never uses `add_note`.
rules.note: add_note must not be called (API marks it Brief B).

rules.quote: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
rules.note: Brief rule 47. Every path, including third-party closes.

open_questions.question: Call on a Saturday or Sunday: 'the last business day of this week' is already past. Not stated.
open_questions.built: Propose the last business day of the following week, checked against rule 19.

open_questions.question: 'This <weekday>' when that weekday of the current week is already past.
open_questions.built: Not recordable (before today); ask for the exact day once, as a vague period under rule 21.

open_questions.question: Customer proposes more than the full past-due amount.
open_questions.built: Do not record above past_due; propose the full past-due amount.

open_questions.question: The third party gives no time at all or does not know when the customer can be reached.
open_questions.built: Treated like an out-of-window offer: ask once more, then not_reached / no_callback without scheduling.

open_questions.question: Is 'today' allowed for a callback when today is not a business day?
open_questions.built: Stricter: today only if it is a business day; otherwise only the next business day.

open_questions.question: A failure (500 or ok=false) of verify_identity, get_account, schedule_callback, transfer_to_agent or close_call. The brief only covers create_promise.
open_questions.built: Retry once (API: the call may be repeated); never claim the action happened; no invented close reason. service_error is used only for rule 37.

open_questions.question: Does proposing the deadline under rule 21 consume a persuasion attempt, and what if it is refused?
open_questions.built: Not an attempt; a refusal of it is a flat refusal as in rule 23.

open_questions.question: Hardship or a plan request raised before identity is verified.
open_questions.built: Rule 1 holds: nothing about the account; continue verification. Only rule 42 (human) is stated to apply before verification.

open_questions.question: days_late outside 1 to 45 returned by get_account.
open_questions.built: 0 or less is not expected; above 45 is treated as the late band (stricter deadline).

open_questions.question: Opening answer 'no' with no further information (not clearly a third party, wrong number or unclear).
open_questions.built: Treated as someone else on the line: section 4.
